ayahOccurrences.text: وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: وَدَاوُۥدَ وَسُلَيْمَٰنَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى ٱلْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ ٱلْقَوْمِ وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَٰهِدِينَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: نَفَشَتْ is in the derivative form: نَفَشَ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ن/ف/ش   n–f–sh wool, to tease out, to ruffle the feathers, to bristle up, to swell, to scatter over a large area. Some scholars attribute an Aramaic origin to the form مَنْفُوشٌ manfūsh.

Of this root, 2 forms occur 1 time each in the Qur’an:
نَفَشَ nafasha and مَنْفُوشٌ manfūsh.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
نَفَشَ nafasha u [v. intrans.] to disperse, (of animals) to stray into a piece of land for grazing

(21:78) وَدَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِى الْحَرْثِ إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ and [remember] David and Solomon, when they arbitrated regarding the field into which the sheep of some people strayed [by night] to graze.

entries.label: مَنْفُوشٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مَنْفُوشٌ manfūsh [pass. part.] teased out, rarefied, carded, tufted

(101:5) وَتَكُونُ الْجِبَالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ and the mountains will be like carded wool.
